message.content:
```bash
ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i frames/%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p output.mp4
```

A few notes on the parts that commonly trip people up:

- **`-framerate 24` must come *before* `-i`** — it sets the input frame rate. Putting `-r 24` after the input instead can cause duplicated/dropped frames.
- **`%04d.png`** matches zero-padded names like `0001.png`. Adjust the padding to your files: `%d.png` for `1.png`, `%03d.png` for `001.png`. If your sequence starts at a number other than 1 (e.g., starts at 7), add `-start_number 7` before `-i`.
- **`-pix_fmt yuv420p`** converts to a pixel format most players (QuickTime, browsers, etc.) can handle — without it you may get a file that plays black or fails on some devices.
- **Quality:** libx264 defaults to CRF 23. Add `-crf 18` (or lower) before the output for higher quality, e.g. `-c:v libx264 -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p`.

If your filenames aren't sequentially numbered, use a glob instead (Linux/macOS):

```bash
ffmpeg -framerate 24 -pattern_type glob -i 'frames/*.png' -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p output.mp4
```

The ffmpeg command to turn a folder of PNG frames into an MP4 at 24 fps:

```bash
ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i frames/%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p output.mp4
```

Key points:
- `-framerate 24` sets the input frame rate (note: this should come BEFORE the `-i` flag so it applies to the input, not output; using `-r` after input can cause frame duplication issues)
- The pattern `%04d.png` matches files numbered like `0001.png`, `0002.png`, etc. Adjust the number of digits to match the actual naming (e.g., `%d.png` for `1.png`, `%03d.png` for `001.png`)
- `-c:v libx264` encodes with H.264
- `-pix_fmt yuv420p` ensures compatibility with most players (many players can't handle yuv444 or RGB)
- Optionally `-crf` for quality (0-51, lower = better, ~18-23 is common)

Some other useful notes:
- If starting number isn't 1, use `-start_number N` before the input
- If files don't start at 1 or have gaps, could use glob pattern: `-pattern_type glob -i 'frames/*.png'`
